question.problem:
Consider the matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 4 & -9 \\ -8 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Determine whether $A=PD{P}^{-1}$ for some invertible matrix $P$ and a diagonal matrix $D,$ where $P$ and $D$ are both real. In the affirmative case, find a possible diagonal matrix $D.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to determine whether $D$ is diagonalizable over $R.$

We start by computing the eigenvalues of $A.$ To do that, we solve the characteristic equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 4-\lambda  & -9 \\ -8 & 0 & -4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & 3 \\ -8 & -4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )((4-\lambda )(-4-\lambda )+24) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+8) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

For the quadratic polynomial $\,{\lambda }^{2}+8\,$ we have that the discriminant $D<0.$ So, it doesn't have real roots. 

Therefore, $A$ is not diagonalizable over $R.$
